biography.plain_text: Daniel W. Crotty is an American businessman and owner of Ritz Safety, a distributor of protective equipment. He succeeded his father in the family's uniform-rental business alongside two brothers. When its rental operations were sold to Cintas, the safety division remained separate, becoming the focus of his subsequent business interests.

confidence.reason: Primary family and corporate accounts support these allocated facts, with company practices explicitly attributed to the enterprise.

long_biography.plain_text:
Daniel Crotty's safety-supply business combines product distribution with services delivered at customers' workplaces. Ritz Safety offers equipment rental, prescription protective eyewear, safety audits and practical training. Its staff participated in a construction association's safety committee, hearing directly from contractors about the equipment they needed and the conditions in which it would be used.

The company also developed custom high-visibility clothing through overseas suppliers and expanded its embroidery facilities. Showrooms and distribution centres supported the regional network, while a training centre opened alongside its Dayton headquarters. A mobile version of its catalogue allowed customers to place orders away from their desks.
